diagnostic_evidence.quote: associated with an uncertainty set $\Theta \subset \mathcal{L} \times \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{S}_+(d)$ satisfying the scaling property (\ref{scale_property})
$(X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ has independent increments, i.e., $X_t - X_s$ is independent from $(X_{t_1}, \ldots, X_{t_n})$

issues.failure_explanation: As written these are pathwise identities. $\xi_t=t\sqrt{\xi_1}$ requires $\xi_1\ge 0$ (false for the symmetric G-Brownian component) and uses the wrong power of $t$; pathwise $\eta_t=t\eta_1$ would make every increment a multiple of $\eta_1$, and independence of increments then forces $\eta_1$ to be deterministic, contradicting mean uncertainty. The correct (standard, and clearly intended) self-similarity is distributional: $\xi_t\overset{d}{=}\sqrt{t}\,\xi_1$, $\eta_t\overset{d}{=}t\eta_1$, $\zeta_t\overset{d}{=}t^{1/\alpha}\zeta_1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the three pathwise identities by distributional equalities with the correct scalings ($\sqrt{t}\xi_1$, $t\eta_1$, $t^{1/\alpha}\zeta_1$).
issues.overall_effect: The property that Theorem \ref{universal limit theorem} attributes to the limiting nonlinear L\'evy process is misstated; no proof in the paper uses \eqref{scale_property}, so nothing downstream is affected.
issues.title: Scaling property stated as pathwise identity with wrong power of t
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of a recalled background property; no argument, estimate, or rate in the paper depends on the erroneous version.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\zeta \in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{d})$ be a nonnegative mollifier with unit integral and compact support in $[-1,0] \times B_{1}$

issues.failure_explanation: Since the time support of $\zeta_\varepsilon$ lies in $(-\varepsilon^2,0)$, the convolution at time $t$ samples $v$ at times $t-\tau\in(t,t+\varepsilon^2)$. For $t\in(1-\varepsilon^2,1]$ this requires $v$ on $(1,1+\varepsilon^2)$, but $v$ (the viscosity solution $u$ or the scheme solution $u_h$) is only defined on $[0,1]$. Hence $v^\varepsilon$ is not well-defined on part of the strip $[h,1]$ where the proof of Theorem \ref{main theorem} uses it, and the convex-combination supersolution argument near $t=1$ would average values beyond the horizon where the PIDE is not known to hold.

failure_location.quote: v^{\varepsilon}(t,x,y,z) := (v \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon})(t,x,y,z) := \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend $u$ to $[0,1+\varepsilon^2]$ via its Feynman--Kac representation $u(t,x,y,z)=\tilde{\mathbb E}[\phi(x+\xi_t,y+\eta_t,z+\zeta_t)]$ (a viscosity solution on the larger horizon with the same regularity) and extend $u_h$ by the same recursion; or restrict the mollified functions to $t\le 1-\varepsilon^2$ and treat the terminal layer separately.
issues.overall_effect: $u^\varepsilon$ and $u_h^\varepsilon$, and with them the key steps \eqref{ueps} and \eqref{uheps}, are not constructed on the whole time interval needed; the proof of Theorem \ref{main theorem} (and hence Theorems \ref{main theorem CLT}, \ref{main theorem ex1}, \ref{main theorem ex1 CLT}) has a definitional gap at the terminal time.
issues.title: Forward-in-time mollification evaluates v beyond the horizon t=1
issues.why_classification: A routine definitional extension that changes no estimate, constant, or rate; every substantive claim survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e)
\| \partial_{t}^{i} D^{j} v^{\varepsilon} \|_{\infty} \leq 2C K_{\zeta} \varepsilon^{1 - 2i - j}, \quad \text{for all } i,j \in \mathbb{N},

issues.failure_explanation: $\zeta$ is a mollifier on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d$ and the convolution subtracts the same $e\in\mathbb{R}^d$ from each of $x,y,z$. Shifts $(x,y,z)\mapsto(x-e,y-e,z-e)$ leave functions of $x-y$ (etc.) invariant: e.g. $v(t,x,y,z)=|x_1-y_1|\wedge 1$ satisfies the stated H\"older--Lipschitz condition with $C=1$, but the integrand is independent of $(\tau,e)$, so $v^\varepsilon=v$, which is not even $C^1$. Pure and mixed partial derivatives such as $D_x^2v^\varepsilon$, $D_{xy}^2v^\varepsilon$, $D_x^3v^\varepsilon$ therefore need not exist, and the claimed bound $\|\partial_t^iD^jv^\varepsilon\|_\infty\le 2CK_\zeta\varepsilon^{1-2i-j}$ for arbitrary derivatives on $\mathbb{R}^{3d}$ is false.

failure_location.quote: It is clear that $v^{\varepsilon} \in C_{b}^{\infty}$, and the standard mollification estimates, together with the regularity of $v$, imply:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Mollify in all $3d$ spatial variables: take $\zeta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{3d})$ and define $v^\varepsilon(t,x,y,z)=\int v(t-\tau,x-e_1,y-e_2,z-e_3)\zeta_\varepsilon(\tau,e_1,e_2,e_3)\,de_1de_2de_3d\tau$ with $\zeta_\varepsilon=\varepsilon^{-(2+3d)}\zeta(\tau/\varepsilon^2,e/\varepsilon)$; all stated estimates and every subsequent argument then go through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem \ref{main theorem} applies Lemma \ref{consistency}, which requires $\omega\in C_b^\infty$ with bounded $D_x^3,D_{xz}^2,D_{xy}^2,\partial_tD_z$, etc., to $u^\varepsilon$ and $u_h^\varepsilon$; the smoothness and the derivative bounds \eqref{u_mollifer} and \eqref{uh_mollifer} are not established, so the error bounds of Theorems \ref{main theorem}, \ref{main theorem CLT}, \ref{main theorem ex1}, \ref{main theorem ex1 CLT} rest on an unproved smoothing step.
issues.title: Mollification in d diagonal directions does not smooth functions on R^{3d}
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line, standard change of mollifier that preserves the form of every estimate and every convergence rate; no new lemma or reoptimization is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated modulus of continuity, the shift $(\tau,e,e,e)$ with $|\tau|<\varepsilon^2$, $|e|<\varepsilon$ gives $|v(t,x,y,z)-v(t-\tau,x-e,y-e,z-e)|\le C(|\tau|^{1/2}+|e|+|e|+|e|)\le 4C\varepsilon$, not $2C\varepsilon$. The same miscount affects the oscillation used in the derivative bounds (which should carry the constant $4CK_\zeta$, not $2CK_\zeta$). Consequently the constants in \eqref{u_mollifer}, \eqref{uh_mollifer}, $E_1$, $E_2$ and the theorem's $\min_\varepsilon(4C_0\varepsilon+E_i)$ are all off by a factor of about two.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $2C\varepsilon$ by $4C\varepsilon$ (and $2CK_\zeta$ by $4CK_\zeta$) in \eqref{v_varp_estimate} and propagate the doubled mollification constants through \eqref{u_mollifer}, \eqref{uh_mollifer}, $E_1,E_2$ and the final bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants appearing in Theorem \ref{main theorem} (and hence in Theorem \ref{main theorem CLT}, whose bound displays $4C_0\varepsilon$) are not the ones delivered by the paper's own estimates; no rate or form of any bound changes.
issues.title: Mollification sup-error constant ignores the three shifted spatial blocks
issues.why_classification: Constant-level corrections only; every rate, regime, and the shape of all error bounds survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: \eqref{E1} and \eqref{E2} define $E_1,E_2$ with the term $\hat l_{u^\varepsilon(t,x,y,z+\cdot)}(h)$ (resp. $u_h^\varepsilon$), which depends on $(t,x,y,z)$: Assumption \ref{assump2}(vi) provides a rate function $\hat l_\varphi$ for each fixed test function $\varphi\in C_b^3$, with no uniformity over the family of $z$-sections of $u^\varepsilon$/$u_h^\varepsilon$. The comparison arguments, however, require scalar error functions: the barrier $\bar u=u_h^\varepsilon+E_1(\varepsilon,h)(t-h)$ is a supersolution only if $E_1$ is constant in $(x,y,z)$, and the theorem statement minimizes over $\varepsilon$ as if $E_i(\varepsilon,h)$ were scalars. As written, the objects $E_i(\varepsilon,h)$ used in the statements are not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $E_i(\varepsilon,h)$ with $\sup_{(t,x,y,z)}\hat l_{u^\varepsilon(t,x,y,z+\cdot)}(h)$ (likewise for $u_h^\varepsilon$) in place of the pointwise term, and note the supremum is finite and $o(1)$ in the examples via \eqref{consistency estimates}.
issues.overall_effect: The bounds of Theorem \ref{main theorem} and Theorem \ref{main theorem CLT} are formally ill-posed in the general (non-example) setting, and the barrier comparison step is unjustified; in the example of Section 4 the consistency estimate \eqref{consistency estimates} controls $\hat l_\varphi$ through $\|D\varphi\|_\infty,\|D^2\varphi\|_\infty$ alone, restoring uniformity, so the application survives.
issues.title: Error functions E_1, E_2 are not scalar functions of (epsilon,h)
issues.why_classification: A definitional/uniformity repair with no loss of content: the paper's concrete application satisfies the needed uniformity automatically, and all rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: In the upper-bound step, Lemma \ref{comparison} is invoked with $\underline\omega=u_h$. But $u_h$, defined recursively by \eqref{approx_scheme}, is piecewise constant in $t$ with jumps of order $h^{1/2}$ at the grid points $t=kh$ (this is exactly why Lemma \ref{uh_regularity}(ii) carries the $+h^{1/2}$ term), so $u_h\notin C_b([0,1]\times\mathbb{R}^{3d})$ and the lemma is applied outside its stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: By the comparison principle (Lemma \ref{comparison}), we have:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Lemma \ref{comparison} for bounded functions that are piecewise constant (or merely right-continuous) in $t$; the inductive proof of such discrete comparison principles (cf. [BJ2007, Lemma 3.2]) applies verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: One step in the proof of Theorem \ref{main theorem}(ii) is unsupported as written; no conclusion changes once the comparison lemma is stated for the class of functions the scheme produces.
issues.title: Discrete comparison lemma applied to the time-discontinuous scheme solution u_h
issues.why_classification: A hypothesis restatement whose proof is unchanged; the step is bypassed with no modification to any estimate or guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma \ref{uh_regularity}(ii) gives $|u_h(t,\cdot)-u_h(s,\cdot)|\le C_0(|t-s|^{1/2}+h^{1/2})$, the $h^{1/2}$ accounting for the jumps of the piecewise-constant-in-time scheme. Hence $\|u_h-u_h^\varepsilon\|_\infty\le 2C_0\varepsilon+C_0h^{1/2}$ (with ISSUE-004's constant, $4C_0\varepsilon+C_0h^{1/2}$), not $2C_0\varepsilon$ as stated in \eqref{uh_mollifer} (the companion derivative bound in the same display does contain the $(\varepsilon+h^{1/2})$ factor, confirming the jump term was overlooked only in the sup bound). The same omission makes property (C1) in Section 2.4 false as stated: at $t=h$, $t'\uparrow h$, the jump is of order $h^{1/2}$ while $|t-t'|^{1/2}\to0$. Consequently, in the proof of part (i) the barrier $\underline u=u-2C_0h^{1/2}-2C_0\varepsilon$ does not satisfy $\underline u(h)\le\bar u(h)$: $u(h)-u_h^\varepsilon(h)\le 2C_0h^{1/2}+(2C_0\varepsilon+C_0h^{1/2})$ exceeds the subtracted amount, so the stated constant $2C_0h^{1/2}$ in Theorem \ref{main theorem}(i) is not delivered (the argument yields $4C_0h^{1/2}$).

failure_location.quote: \|u_h - u_h^{\varepsilon}\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_0 \varepsilon, \quad \|\partial_t^l D_x^k u_h^{\varepsilon}\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_0 K_{\zeta} (\varepsilon + h^{1/2}) \varepsilon^{-2l-k}, \quad \forall k,l \in \mathbb{N}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the corrected estimate $\|u_h-u_h^\varepsilon\|_\infty\le 2C_0\varepsilon+C_0h^{1/2}$, enlarge the barrier to $\underline u=u-3C_0h^{1/2}-2C_0\varepsilon$, adjust the final constant in part (i) to $4C_0h^{1/2}$, and add the $+h^{1/2}$ term in (C1).
issues.overall_effect: The constant in front of $h^{1/2}$ in Theorem \ref{main theorem}(i), and hence in the lower bound of Theorem \ref{main theorem CLT}, is wrong; the form of the bounds and every convergence rate survive.
issues.title: Mollifier error for u_h drops the h^{1/2} grid-jump term (and (C1) is false)
issues.why_classification: The repair only enlarges constants in front of an already-present $h^{1/2}$ term; the method, the shape of the error bounds, and all rates are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, for sufficiently small \( h > 0 \), we have:
Setting \( h = \frac{1}{n} \) and \( (t,x,y,z) = (1, 0, 0, 0) \), it follows from Theorem \ref{main theorem} that

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem \ref{main theorem CLT} asserts the two-sided bound for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, but it is deduced from Theorem \ref{main theorem} with $h=1/n$, and that theorem is only established for sufficiently small $h$, i.e., for sufficiently large $n$. No argument is given that the finitely many remaining small $n$ satisfy the bound with the displayed constants $2C_0n^{-1/2}$ and $4C_0\varepsilon$.

failure_location.quote: for all \( n \in \mathbb{N} \), where the functions \( E_1 \) and \( E_2 \) are defined in Theorem \ref{main theorem}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound for all sufficiently large $n$, or note that the finitely many remaining $n$ are absorbed by enlarging the constants.
issues.overall_effect: The stated scope (validity for every $n$) is unestablished; the asymptotic rate content is unaffected.
issues.title: Berry--Esseen bound stated for all n although the main theorem covers only sufficiently small h
issues.why_classification: A scope/quantifier adjustment with no change to the rate or the method; the result survives verbatim for large $n$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This yields the lower bound for $\delta$, given by $\delta > \alpha \frac{q_1}{2} \geq \frac{3}{4}\alpha$. The upper bound for $\delta$ is standard

issues.failure_explanation: With $q_1=3/2$ (imposed by $M_{X_1}^3<\infty$ via $p_1=3$), the estimate used is the interpolation $\min(A,B)^{q_1}\le A^{q_1-\delta}B^\delta$ with $A=2\|D_x\omega\|_\infty$ and $B=\|D_{xz}^2\omega\|_\infty h^{1/\alpha}|Z|$. For $\delta>q_1$ this inequality is false in general (e.g., $A=100$, $B=1$, $q_1=3/2$, $\delta=1.7$ gives $1\le 100^{-0.2}$), and in context $B\ll A$ on the event $\{|Z|\le \|D_x\omega\|/(\|D_{xz}^2\omega\|h^{1/\alpha})\}$. The argument therefore needs $\delta\le 3/2$, but Assumption (v) and Remark \ref{remark_delta} impose only $\delta<\alpha$ from above, so for $\alpha\in(3/2,2)$ the admissible range contains $\delta\in(3/2,\alpha)$ (realized in the examples, where $M_{Z_1}^\delta<\infty$ for all $\delta<\alpha$). For such $\delta$ the lemma's stated factor $\|D_x\omega\|_\infty^{(3-2\delta)/3}$ has a negative exponent, and the derivations of $E_1,E_2$ in Theorem \ref{main theorem} bound this negative power by upper mollifier estimates in the wrong direction (e.g., the term $\varepsilon^{-2\delta/3}h^{(4\delta-3\alpha)/(6\alpha)}$ in \eqref{E2}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Assumption (v) to $\delta\in(\frac{3}{4}\alpha\vee1,\,\alpha\wedge\frac32]$ (nonempty for all $\alpha\in(1,2)$; lower-order moments are finite by Lyapunov) and replace $\delta$ by $\delta\wedge\frac32$ in the first term of $\Gamma$ in Theorems \ref{main theorem ex1} and \ref{main theorem ex1 CLT}; for $\delta>3/2$ the cross term becomes $h^{1/\alpha-1/2}\|D_{xz}^2\omega\|_\infty$ with constraint $\gamma\le(2-\alpha)/(4\alpha)$.
issues.overall_effect: For $\alpha>3/2$ and $\delta\in(3/2,\alpha)$ the consistency lemma is unproved and the error functions $E_1,E_2$ of Theorem \ref{main theorem} are not established as written; consequently the explicit rate $\Gamma(\alpha,\delta,q_0)$ in Theorems \ref{main theorem ex1} and \ref{main theorem ex1 CLT} is overstated in that subregime (its first term should be capped at $\delta=3/2$, giving $(2-\alpha)/(4\alpha)$ instead of $(4\delta-3\alpha)/(2\alpha(2\delta+3))$).
issues.title: Interpolation in the consistency proof requires delta <= 3/2, but the admissible range allows delta > 3/2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained parameter restriction plus reoptimization needing no new proof architecture, and for $\alpha\le 3/2$ nothing changes; but in the subregime $\alpha>3/2$, $\delta>3/2$ the advertised rate exponent strictly worsens (e.g., from $\approx 0.071$ to $\approx 0.014$ near $\alpha=2$), which is more than a local or constant-level fix while leaving a recognizably comparable explicit polynomial rate.
